name: The relationship between domestic violence and shooting incidents in New York City
description: This dataset examines the relationship between domestic violence and shooting incidents across New York City police precincts. Each row represents a precinct or location type and includes counts of shootings and overall domestic violence incidents, along with precinct population figures and corresponding rates per population. The data also breaks down actual versus expected shooting and domestic violence counts by race and ethnicity (white, black, Asian/Pacific Islander, American Indian, and other) and by sex (male and female), alongside citywide population figures for each group. With 83 sampled rows and 43 columns, the dataset supports analysis of how domestic violence levels relate to gun violence geographically, and whether shootings and domestic violence incidents are distributed across demographic groups in proportion to their share of the population. It could be useful for public safety researchers, policy analysts, and community organizations studying crime patterns, resource allocation, or disparities in policing outcomes.
